canonical_claim: B33's former Replicated-on-CA restriction is lifted; Replicated on a CA disk is now supported end-to-end.
A confirmed relink is not proven dangle-free when a listing page is incomplete; `CaRelinkConfirmCore.tla` produces a counterexample and `ca-fsck` is the backstop.

A replica restart could remain permanently readonly when a CA part was committed but ZK-unknown, `republishRef` adopted a blob whose token was condemned in a fresh retire view, and `promote` aborted without an attach retry.

Two replicas performing the same shared-pool `OPTIMIZE FINAL` independently can double-spill roughly one full part size each even though deduplication retains one pool blob; a shared-pool replica could adopt the already-uploaded blob instead of re-merging locally.

The existing replicated-merge exponential backoff is defeated when CAS uses `ABORTED`: `ReplicatedMergeMutateTaskBase` treats `ABORTED` as deliberate cancellation, so `last_exception_time_ms` remains zero and a failed merge can be recomputed in a tight loop. Additionally, The tight merge loop was not caused by an absent queue backoff: `ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue::getPostponeTimeMsForEntry` already computes exponential backoff, but CAS `ABORTED` is exempted from `updateLastExeption`, leaving `last_exception_time_ms=0` and the computed postpone at zero.

When a MERGE exception escapes `commit()`, orchestration cancels and releases the task, `ContentAddressedTransaction` removes the staging key, and the replication scheduler later selects and recomputes the whole merge; INSERT instead surfaces the failure to its query caller.

The fetch-by-relink exposure is limited to a short synchronous `stageManifest` window before `precommitAdd`. Additionally, Review finding №6 is real: a sender can release its source part while a receiver's `precommitAdd` edge PUT is stalled across at least two GC folds, allowing the only same-token blob reference to be reclaimed. Additionally, Relink handoff retention requires a sender-created build-owned epoch-floor pin that remains until the receiver's edge is durable; otherwise a same-token blob can be reclaimed during a stalled handoff. Additionally, Fetch-by-relink can promote a manifest naming a deleted blob because the sender has no retention pin while the receiver waits to publish its precommit edge. Additionally, Same-pool fetch-by-relink can leave the receiver with a dangling committed manifest if the receiver's `precommitAdd` edge is not durable before the sender's now-`Outdated` part is collected. Additionally, Relink replication can delete blobs during the sender-to-receiver gap because the sender releases its source edge before receiver precommit and no durable handoff or pin spans receiver commit.

Review finding №7 is real: the receiver compares the advertised pool only on the sender, so a reservation can select a non-CA disk or a different CA pool and publish a dangling manifest or throw before byte fallback. Additionally, A receiver must compare the reservation-selected disk's CA pool UUID with the advertised pool UUID and use byte fallback for either a non-CA disk or a different pool. Additionally, After fetch reservation, a relink is allowed only when the chosen disk is CA and its pool UUID equals the advertised pool UUID; otherwise the code must invoke the existing byte-fetch fallback. Additionally, Relink can advertise pool A while reservation selects a local disk or pool B, allowing pool B to publish references to bodies that exist only in A.

The smoking-gun log says `Block with ID all_10341432382904313846_13999145979494917125 already exists on other replicas as part all_1117_1117_0; ignoring it.`, while `all_1117_1117_0` was absent from both replicas. Additionally, R3's `NETWORK_ERROR` with `retry-later` caused a byte-identical retry to reuse the same `block_id`; cross-replica dedup found the phantom znode and returned success without inserting rows. Additionally, The refined root cause is that the `block_id` and part-znode survive removal of a part whose CA blob PUTs failed, so the surviving block-id znode outlives CAS-blob durability and falsely deduplicates a byte-identical retry. Additionally, After the first attempt, Keeper contains the block-id and part-znode while no replica contains part data, creating a phantom part. Additionally, On the retry, `getActiveContainingPart` returns null, so the existing block-id is treated as cross-replica dedup and the server emits `INSERT_WAS_DEDUPLICATED` with HTTP 200 despite inserting no rows. Additionally, A surviving `block_id` has an independent rolling `replicated_deduplication_window`, so a byte-identical retry can be acknowledged as deduplicated after the phantom part-znode is cleaned. Additionally, The data-loss trace found `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::commitPart` ordering `renameParts()` as an overlay re-key, then Keeper block-id/part-znode commit, then CA `publishStaging`; a failure between the Keeper multi and CA publish creates a split-commit window. Additionally, In the split-commit window, a surviving Keeper block ID can make a byte-identical retry appear deduplicated even though the part's data was never durably published, producing an acknowledged but lost insert while `fsck` remains clean. Additionally, The same Keeper-before-storage durability violation exists in upstream plain-S3: local metadata operations, including temporary-to-final rename, are queued until `transaction.commit` after the Keeper multi, so a crash can leave a phantom part and surviving block ID that silently acknowledges a retry.

The S37 duplicate-part result was pre-existing rather than an R2 regression: a killed `MOVE PARTITION` run produced `count=200` and `uniqExact=100`, while the R2 MOVE-to-CA operation itself had `mover_error=None`; the issue was backlogged as generic replication or MOVE behavior.

After a relink `adoptPartFromManifest` publishes a `tmp-fetch_` ref, a later local exception in `Fetcher::relinkPartToDisk` may leave a published ref without a loaded part unless startup cleanup is proven to reap it.
The older `test_replicated_fetch_by_relink` test was green for the wrong reason because its flat `count_blobs()` assertion cannot distinguish relink from a deduplicating byte fetch.
Forbidding `Ordinary` with CAS would break replicated recovery because the broken-tables path deliberately creates an `Ordinary` database to discard a table UUID.

Relink races GC in the shared pool (RPL-3): between the sender encoding a manifest and the receiver's `promote`, GC on the shared pool can condemn a blob that was live via the sender's ref; this is a TOCTOU inside promote in the same window as the general J1 zombie-writer/X1 reader-pin class, mitigated in practice by GC's two-phase graduation (`delete_pending` before `deleteExact`) plus copy-forward, but not provably closed for the relink promote path and has no dedicated test.

A CA relink is advertised only for `try_zero_copy && !to_detached`, preventing byte-fetch fallback loops and ensuring detached fetches use the detached namespace. Additionally, `to_detached` relink is disabled and `FETCH PARTITION` always streams bytes (RPL-4): the receiver only advertises relink when `try_zero_copy && !to_detached`, so `ALTER TABLE ... FETCH PARTITION` (into `detached/`) and the byte-fetch fallback never relink — they stream full bytes even within the same pool, then content-address and dedup on landing. This is correct but a performance cliff, explicitly deferred in code as "Relink-into-detached is a deferred optimization".

`DataPartsExchange.cpp:1084` calls `ContentAddressed::parseTableUuid` directly instead of going through the `IContentAddressedExchange` facade the relink design established, coupling core `MergeTree` code to a concrete CA helper's signature; the fix is to derive the table uuid inside `adoptPartFromManifest`, which already knows the receiver namespace. Additionally, Risk register #12 (Medium, confirmed): `DataPartsExchange.cpp:1084` calls `parseTableUuid` directly, bypassing the intended facade, and the `IContentAddressedExchange` seam header lives inside the feature directory, so core code compile-depends on a feature-dir header — the one break in an otherwise clean inward-only dependency direction. Suggested action: move uuid derivation into `adoptPartFromManifest`; relocate the interface header.

Risk register #16 (Low, confirmed): the `DataPartsExchange` relink payload rides manifest bytes over the legacy `part_id` cookie field, explicitly documented as "no protocol field changes on this branch" — fine intra-branch, but a release needs a real dedicated wire field.

`MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts`'s unconditional pre-Keeper-commit disk-transaction close (the R3 acked-then-lost fix) reorders durability for ALL `DiskObjectStorage`-backed MergeTree writes, not just CAS, and needs dedicated non-CA regression coverage (plain S3 + `ReplicatedMergeTree`, zero-copy) and its own standalone upstream presentation.
Same-pool replica relinking transfers manifest information without blob bytes and requires matching content_addressed_pool_uuid; otherwise the receiver uses byte-fetch fallback.
CAS is enabled per disk with metadata_type = content_addressed, and zero-copy replication remains available but is mutually exclusive with CAS per disk.

A stable minted pool_uuid in _pool_meta is the same-pool criterion for fetch-by-relink; endpoint and prefix string matching is rejected because it can produce false-positive relinks and dangling refs.
`REPLICATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION_WITH_CA_RELINK` is protocol version 10; mixed-version clusters negotiate the minimum version and automatically fall back to byte transfer.
The CA relink wire contract sends `pool_uuid` and encoded `PartManifest` bytes in the legacy `part_id` cookie as `part_manifest_v1`; sender identity fields in the body are non-authoritative.
Same-pool CA replication transfers a manifest instead of blob bytes; the receiver adopts shared-pool blobs into a fresh receiver-local manifest and publishes its own ref.
If CA manifest adoption fails because a referenced blob is missing or condemned, the receiver publishes nothing and retries the fetch with `try_zero_copy=false`.
The `part_id` cookie in `ContentAddressedExchange.h` remains a reachable legacy compatibility field in the replicated-fetch exchange.

Within one pool, `BACKUP` is a per-disk snapshot, consolidation makes a selected snapshot pool-complete, mirror copies snapshots to a backup pool, fetch selectively pulls closures, and `RESTORE` relinks refs locally.

The mirror daemon runs on the backup side, reads production with read-only credentials, writes with backup credentials, lists only `cas/refs/`, copies missing snapshot-closure objects, and never propagates deletions.
No restore path writes to the backup pool; selective fetch copies a chosen snapshot closure into a fresh or living pool and local `RESTORE` republishes refs with zero data bytes.

The backup invariants are `BAK-RO` for no restore writes to backup, `BAK-EDGE-DRIVEN-MANIFESTS` for edge-only reclamation, `BAK-THIN-AFTER-MIRROR` for ordering, `BAK-INDEPENDENT-RETENTION` for destination retention, and `BAK-NO-IDENTITY-COPY` for identity objects.

Relink promotion is authorized only by literal `yes`; missing, unknown, timeout, and transport-error outcomes are locally generated `NETWORK_ERROR` retry outcomes rather than byte-fetch success. Additionally, The typed relink boundary treats confirm `no`, `unknown`, and transport failure as `SourceProofFailed`: it aborts and throws a locally generated retry-later error rather than returning `false` for same-sender byte fallback. Additionally, The confirm wire is binary and fail-closed: only `yes` authorizes, while `No`, `Unknown`, and an absent cookie are all treated as unproven; old receivers ignore the unknown cookie and old senders offer relink without a token. Additionally, `prepareAdoptFromManifest` returns `Prepared` or `MechanismFallbackAllowed`; a confirm failure is not mechanism fallback, so the receiver must abort and throw a retry-later `NETWORK_ERROR` rather than byte-fetching on an unproven source. Additionally, In receiver state S2, an unresolved promotion must retry later and never fetch bytes, because a byte fetch could publish a part twice over a relink that may already have committed. Additionally, A relink refusal throws `NETWORK_ERROR`, is stored for retry-later with backoff and reselection, and must not issue a byte re-request to the same source; the path therefore cannot duplicate bytes or double-publish.

`mutateShard` is synchronous for its caller, so every queued mutation is a blocked thread waiting on a promise and the total queued items across all shards is bounded by the number of concurrently writing threads.
A cross-server CAS conflict causes the queue leader to re-read and re-apply all not-yet-completed closures, while exhaustion of `MAX_CAS_ATTEMPTS` fails every promise in the batch.
The queued flush applies the soft-limit delay once per flush whenever any batched item has `origin == Writer`, preserving the pacing intent tracked by B164b.
S12 ten-replica shared-pool validation showed byte-identical convergence, `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided=40`, and `dangling=0` under concurrent inserts.

Local-source relinks hold the source as a live `DataPartPtr`, so the source replica's edge remains pinned through the destination commit and the exposure is structurally unreachable for those relinks.
CAS refs are per-replica while blobs are pool-wide, so a blob's in-degree counts one edge for each replica manifest that names it.
`metadata_version.txt` is write-once in current live writers and may legitimately diverge across replicas during `ALTER` metadata-snapshot windows.
The planned manifest-trust promote path removes per-leaf `head` and `loadMeta` probes for adopted leaves and emits `CasBlobAdoptTrusted` with `reason=manifest-trust`.
Reader pin tokens are advanceable: parts still present in a refreshed snapshot advance to the new snapshot, while dropped-but-held parts retain their last valid snapshot.
Reader retention is unbounded by a separate `H_max`; active query duration and reader lease TTL are the intended retention bounds.
The reader design requires the `IDataPartStorage::snapshot_pin` hook to be nullable and disk-gated so non-CAS and non-reader disks receive `nullptr`.

`Fetcher::relinkPartToDisk` reconstructs a fetched part solely from the transferred manifest; its `part_uuid` and `metadata_version` parameters and `sidecar_values` block are removed, and the relink cookie changes from `part_manifest_v1` to `part_manifest_v2`.
In the superseded handoff protocol, the sender returned the manifest address and pin ID in the existing response, and the receiver deleted the pin only after its own ref commit.
Under the superseded protocol, a failed sender pin PUT aborted relink and used byte-stream fetch, while a sender or receiver failure left the pin to be reaped rather than risking data loss.

The existing replicated flow remains `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` → `Keeper::tryMultiNoThrow` → `MergeTreeData::Transaction::commit` → `IDataPartStorage::commitTransaction`; the one-pipeline design does not change those call sites. Additionally, If a process terminates after a successful `Keeper` multi but before disk commit, existing recovery finds the missing part, fetches it from another replica when possible, or invokes `onPartIsLostForever` and `createEmptyPartInsteadOfLost` while accounting `lost_part_count`. Additionally, When a post-`Keeper`-multi disk commit fails, ordinary recovery may enqueue the missing part for replica fetch or call `createEmptyPartInsteadOfLost` with `lost_part_count` incremented; the CA design adds no CA-specific recovery mechanism.
A confirm token contains `{pool_uuid, server_root_id, root_namespace, ref_name, part_name, ManifestRef}`; `server_root_id` is required because a pool UUID can be shared across server roots.

Authoritative gate 1 takes `ref_queue_mutex`, pins the resident runtime, then takes `state_mutex` as one snapshot; it returns `yes` only for a warm, live, quiescent, unpoisoned table whose committed `ref_name` row exactly matches the token's `ManifestRef` and whose mount fence is live.
Gate 1 returns `unknown` for a cold, recovering, superseded, nonresident, poisoned, wedged, pending, leader-active, or mid-tenure table, and performs no object-store I/O.

`MechanismFallbackAllowed` remains the byte fallback for version or cookie mismatch, manifest decode failure, or receiver-side publish or promote conflict; mixed versions degrade to bytes and never to unconfirmed relink.

The new `confirm_ca_ref` interserver action carries the exact token in a second authenticated HTTP request after the relink response is consumed, and responses are `yes`, `no`, or `unknown`; transport errors map to `SourceProofFailed`.

The exchange-level gate-0 resolver returns `Unknown` for zero or multiple namespace matches and otherwise requires the named part to be `Active` or `Outdated` on the matched instance's disk, including the same-name `MOVE ... TO DISK` case.

Normal-class ref mutation items cannot split across chunks: an item exceeding `ref_txn_max_ops` is refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` before object creation, while an item that would overflow a non-empty chunk rolls the chunk and lands whole in a fresh one. Additionally, Removal-class items are exempt from the normal op cap but carve solo as `WholeShard` mutations, so they cannot be split by a chunk boundary; their size is bounded by `ref_removal_max_bytes`.

The old busy-lane refusal throws `NETWORK_ERROR`, so the replication queue stores the fetch, backs off, and re-selects a source; it causes convergence latency and log/CPU noise but not duplicate bytes or a double publish.

The relink wire vocabulary uses request parameters `content_addressed_confirm` and `content_addressed_expected`, response cookies `content_addressed_identity`, `content_addressed_answer`, and `content_addressed_nonce`, and `Cache-Control: no-store` on both responses.

`content_addressed_confirm` selects confirm mode and carries the nonce; `content_addressed_expected` carries the adopted validator; `content_addressed_answer` is emitted only by confirm mode; and `unknown:<reason>` is one opaque value that is never parsed or authorized.

Each confirm carries 16 random bytes as the value of `content_addressed_confirm`, and the sender must echo them in `content_addressed_nonce`; absent or mismatched nonces make the result `Unknown` and prevent replay of an earlier response.

The sender's answer vocabulary is `proven` with a matching identity, `changed` with a present different identity, or `unknown:<reason>` with no identity; an absent or unrecognized answer is also `Unknown`.

A part that has disappeared entirely has no binding and therefore produces `Unknown`, not authoritative `changed`; the receiver retries and redoes source and covering-part discovery rather than treating absence as a byte-fetch decision.

A `changed` answer with a present different identity aborts the prepared relink and fetches bytes from the same sender; every other refusal, transport failure, timeout, older peer, or missing part aborts and throws retry-later `NETWORK_ERROR` without a same-sender byte request.
In S0, no ref is published but a staged precommit may remain; the receiver returns `nullptr` and byte-fetches from the same sender with `allow_ca_relink=false` as the recursion brake.

Exact-ref certification is allowed only in `Ready`; `Wedged` and `NeedsRecovery` cannot produce either `Yes` or `No` certification answers. Additionally, Relink certifies only a source view in `Ready`, the receiver promotes only the exact certified identity, and source deletion follows receiver ownership; composition is checked independently by `CaRelinkLaneComposition.tla`.
A relink validator must qualify a binding with namespace, `disk_name`, and `ManifestRef`; equal namespaces on different CAS disks are a collision case when `disk_name` is omitted.
The sender's certified answer and returned identity are separate response fields, and the receiver accepts a relink only when both are independently consistent with the held validator.
A single sender tenure can commit multiple durable chunks of kinds `tracked` and `unrelated`; a `tracked` chunk changes the binding under test, while an `unrelated` chunk does not.

`CasRefLedger::confirmExactRef` snapshots both lane mutexes in order, `ref_queue_mutex` then `state_mutex`, using try-to-lock; admission is therefore wholly before or wholly after the snapshot and cannot be admitted while the function answers `Yes`.

The current confirm rules are rule 2 residency and warmth, rule 3 lane quiescence, rule 4 poison, rule 5 exact row equality as the only `No`, and rule 6 mount fence last; rule 3 currently refuses when `rt.wedge.has_value() || !rt.pending.empty() || rt.leader_active`.

`RefMutationItem.build_ops` materializes operations only at flush, but admission-time `MutationScope` already identifies `Kind::Ref` with one `ref_name` and `Kind::WholeShard`; the batch builder flushes WholeShard operations alone and admits at most one mutation per ref name per flush.

The replication part-fetch HTTP names are `cas_pool_uuid`, `cas_relink`, `cas_confirm`, `cas_source_token`, and `cas_confirm_answer`, and mixed-build clusters must be fully rebuilt because version skew silently falls back to non-CAS full copies. Additionally, The replication wire-protocol literals are cas_pool_uuid, cas_relink, cas_confirm, cas_source_token, and cas_confirm_answer; both protocol sides are in DataPartsExchange.cpp, so mixed-build clusters fall back to full copies. Additionally, The naming plan changes the five part-fetch protocol literals in `DataPartsExchange.cpp` atomically within one build and updates integration-test assertions to match them.

A relink refusal is returned as retry-later `NETWORK_ERROR`; the replication queue requeues and reselects the fetch, and the receiver must not re-request bytes from the same source because that would be unsound.

Same-pool fetch-by-relink detection must use a stable minted `pool_uuid` stored in `_pool_meta`, not endpoint-and-prefix string matching, because aliases can cause false negatives and shared proxies can cause false positives that relink to absent blobs.
Whole-part partition cloning for ATTACH, REPLACE, and MOVE PARTITION on the same disk uses one ref to the source `part_id` and performs zero byte copying.
A Created-then-moved-fence recovery hole transfers exact known durability to `NeedsRecovery` instead of losing the durable transaction.
The relink composition seam requires confirmation in `Ready`, promotion using the exact confirmed identity, and source deletion only with receiver ownership.
`ConfirmedRelinkNeverDangles` guarantees that a promoted receiver with answer `yes` and a durable receiver `+1` before confirmation references only live blobs.

The relink protocol must durably publish the receiver's `+1` before calling confirm; a confirm before that evidence exists does not protect the later promotion. Additionally, Fetch-by-relink follows publish-then-confirm-then-promote: the receiver first durably publishes its own `+1`, then performs one read-only `confirmExactRef`, and promotes only on `yes`. Additionally, The relink receiver protocol is publish → confirm → promote: the receiver durably publishes its `+1`, performs one read-only interserver query proving the sender still has the exact committed manifest binding, and promotes only after that proof succeeds. Additionally, The publish-confirm relink protocol publishes the receiver manifest and precommit first, then asks the sender's lane-linearized `confirmExactRef` about the exact `ManifestRef`, promoting only on a yes and retrying through the replication queue on no or unknown.
A confirm `yes` requires exact `ManifestRef` equality between the sender's committed row and the durable binding at confirmation time.
A confirm must require sender-lane quiescence for the whole tenure, including absence of pending work and an active leader.
A poisoned sender apply must cause confirm to return `unknown`, even if the tenure has closed and the lane appears quiescent.
The writer protocol uses mount startup with `server_root_id` owner claim, durable-monotone `writer_epoch` and `build_sequence`, and the build → precommit → upload → promote sequence.

S12 requires at most one GC leader to make progress per round, duplicate leaders to cause no wrong deletes, and shared physical blob bytes to remain near unique content bytes rather than `replica_count * content_bytes`.
S18 requires a frozen shadow namespace to keep blobs alive independently of live table refs until `SYSTEM UNFREEZE` releases the shadow refs.
S20 requires follower replicas to publish their own refs and sidecars without reuploading existing large blobs, so pool growth is metadata-only per replica.
For CA disks, `supportZeroCopyReplication()==false` while `supportsHardLinks()==true`; unsupported operations are rejected by independent gates, while mutations use whole-part transactions.
A `ReplicatedMergeTree` table is materialized per replica, so a decommission test must create the table on the victim replica to create that replica's local namespace.
A `ReplicatedMergeTree` `DROP` is per replica rather than automatically cluster-wide, so hidden `Removing` catalog entries require dropping the table on both replicas before killing the victim.

The fetch-by-relink protocol uses `REPLICATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION_WITH_CA_RELINK`, `CA_POOL_UUID_PARAM`, and `CA_RELINK_COOKIE`; matching `pool_uuid` values let a same-pool fetch publish a local ref over shared blobs without sending bytes, while non-CA fetches retain their existing behavior.

A DR replica option is a `ReplicatedMergeTree` replica in another region with its own pool; fetch-by-relink applies only within one pool (`pool_uuid` equality), so a foreign-pool replica performs honest byte fetches, giving RPO ~ replication lag and RTO ~0, and covering T1/T4 but not T2 (it replicates `DROP TABLE` too).

ReplicatedMergeTree/CAS ref divergence on partial commit (RPL-2): ZooKeeper is the source of truth for the part set while CAS refs are the source of truth for bytes, and these are two independent commit points with no cross-transaction. If a replica adds a part to ZK but crashes before the CAS ref promote lands, the part is "known" but `resolveRef` returns absent, triggering a re-fetch (recoverable). The converse (CAS-has/ZK-missing) produces an orphaned live ref: reachable and keeping its blobs alive, but invisible to the table — a silent storage leak until DROP TABLE reclaims the namespace.

The relink protocol's defense against an actively-forged affirmative confirm answer relies on the request/response shape being structurally opaque to caches, not on cache policy alone: both legs are POST (not cacheable absent freshness metadata that is never sent), `Cache-Control: no-store` (not `no-cache`) is pinned on both responses to forbid storage entirely rather than permit storage-with-revalidation, and interserver authentication runs before the shared handler dispatches to any endpoint.
The chosen CAS-native backup is a second CAS pool receiving snapshot ref-sets and their hash closures, copying only destination-missing blobs with server-side `CopyObject`.

Frequent multi-disk snapshots are per-disk native snapshots, while consolidation asynchronously uploads hot-tier snapshot hardlinks through the ordinary write path and publishes a pool-complete shadow `_snap`.
Mirroring pinned snapshot closures avoids a source GC race; a live-tail replicator holding a lease was rejected because it would add a GC-wedging actor.

The shard mutation queue is owned by `Store` as one `std::unordered_map<ShardKey, ShardMutationQueue>` protected by one `std::mutex`; an idle queue entry is created by its first waiter and erased by the leader after draining, so an idle pool has no persistent per-prefix queue structures.

The caller that inserts into an idle shard queue becomes its leader; the leader repeatedly carves a batch prefix under the map mutex, releases the mutex for one read-apply-all-CAS cycle, completes promises, and then repeats until the queue is empty.
A queue batch stops before a second mutation of the same `Ref` name and before any `WholeShard` item; `WholeShard` operations such as trim, the GC fence, and `dropNamespace` flush alone.
When a batched final body exceeds the hard limit, the queue degrades to single-item re-flushes so only the offending mutation receives `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and innocent mutations proceed.
The writer owns table semantics and snapshots, while GC owns ref-log folding and physical cleanup; ordinary writer mutations do not read `gc/state` or wait for a GC round.

CAS relink-by-manifest has the same trust model as ordinary `ReplicatedMergeTree` interserver part fetch: the interserver channel is the trust boundary, and table-level RBAC is not a per-blob ACL. Additionally, An umbrella review of the cas-gc-rebuild branch flagged a table-level RBAC/confidentiality-bypass finding in the fetch-by-relink path (a peer could bind any live pool blob into a low-privilege table via wire-supplied manifest entries). This finding was later retracted as not-a-bug: the interserver channel is the same trust boundary an ordinary ReplicatedMergeTree part fetch already has, and this is documented in code rather than fixed as a vulnerability.
Manifest-trust relink adoption trusts only tokenless dependencies marked `DepEntry.adopted`; a tokenless pending-upload dependency remains fail-closed at promote.
Each in-use `DataPart` in reader mode owns an opaque `snapshot_pin` token for its lifetime, and the reader publishes the minimum snapshot over its live tokens as `S_min`.
The all-tree CAS change must not modify `ReplicatedMergeTree` or Keeper formats.

`NETWORK_ERROR` was chosen for CAS retry-later failures because it is outside the merge exemption set, participates in ClickHouse's transient retry taxonomy, and does not receive conflicting special handling on the CAS commit path.

After `uploadFromSource` maps an unresolved conditional create to `NETWORK_ERROR`, `putBlob` no longer retries that fence-lost or unresolved case eight times locally; it escapes to merge-level backoff on the first outer attempt.

Gate 0 is only a part-anchored availability filter: it may return a conservative `no` for absent, `Deleting`, or wrong-disk parts, but a `yes` never proves that no removal was initiated and is authorized solely by gate 1.

B66b uses a dedicated `allow_ca_relink` capability independent of `try_fetch_shared`; every same-sender byte fallback clears `allow_ca_relink` to prevent recursive relink loops, while legacy `try_zero_copy` behavior remains unchanged. Additionally, `allow_ca_relink` is an explicit capability separate from `try_zero_copy`; every byte-fallback re-request passes `allow_ca_relink=false` to prevent persistent mechanism failure from recursively relinking.

The sender mints the source token from the same resolution that obtains the manifest bytes; a second lookup could allow a repoint between offer and mint and authorize a token for a manifest whose entries were not adopted.

The `INVALID_STATE` deposition family at `CasRefLedger.cpp:2041,2312,2892` is intentionally left unchanged: it is on the Write plane, has no destructive consumer, and currently receives queue backoff because `INVALID_STATE` is absent from `ReplicatedMergeMutateTaskBase.cpp:65-78`'s exemption set.

The relink redesign replaces the separate confirm action with a second original offer request to the same endpoint, carrying the same `part` and pool identity plus an opaque validator and per-confirm nonce; it removes the six-field source token, its codec, namespace routing predicate, parts-set gate, and `CasConfirmAnswer` seam type.

The v12 relink design deletes v11's lane-quiescence terms from rule 3 only after representing an apply-pending marker with separate stored and reader-visible values, including the bounded retry in `CasRefLedger::resolveWedgeOnce`.

The T14 report ranks stopping ERROR-severity expected relink refusals as a non-protocol, low-risk optimization, while the underlying `confirmExactRef` rule-3 availability fix remains user-gated because it changes the handoff protocol assertion.

The only intended relaxation of rule 3 is to stop blocking unrelated refs: a wedge remains table-scoped, while a pending named mutation blocks only the matching ref and `WholeShard` blocks all refs; recovery, poison, and fence refusals remain fail-closed.

The planned availability outcome is close to 100% on busy writers except for true same-ref conflicts, `WholeShard` windows, and wedges; the refusal storm and its exception cost should disappear while convergence latency drops to the unrefused path.

A shared-pool replica independently re-merging and re-spilling the same `OPTIMIZE FINAL` work can consume about 186 GiB local scratch to produce one deduplicated 100 GiB blob; the proposed design is to adopt the leader's already-uploaded content-addressed blob instead.

Cross-replica manifest divergence is benign for correctness because single-producer publication is only an optimization; commit-time `checkEqual` is tolerant, and this rationale governs the `manifest_hash` TODO. Additionally, Single-producer non-divergence enforced via a /merge_claims lease plus manifest_hash re-keying (v2 design) was replaced in v3 by tolerant-mode cross-replica commit checking: checkPartChecksumsAndCommit -> checkEqual(..., check_uncompressed_hash_in_compressed_files=true) compares uncompressed hashes, so two replicas with identical uncompressed content but different compressed bytes both pass, yielding at worst two manifests plus two blob sets for one part name (a benign dedup-miss, not a correctness bug; both sets are GC'd when the part is superseded).
`ContentAddressedExchange` replication transfers manifest bytes and lets the receiver adopt listed blobs by hash without payload transfer; decode or promote failure falls back to ordinary byte fetch.

The `manifest_hash` field on the Keeper `/parts` znode was rejected because replication remains disk-agnostic; the manifest ID travels in-band during fetch and manifest divergence is benign. Additionally, The old CA Keeper `manifest_hash` proposal was rejected because it would couple replication to one disk implementation; fetch-by-relink learns the manifest id in-band and manifest divergence is a bounded dedup miss. Additionally, The replication `manifest_hash`-on-Keeper-znode idea B1 was rejected on 2026-07-14 because the manifest id travels in-band and replication remains disk-agnostic. Additionally, A manifest_hash-on-znode idea (B1) to detect cross-replica manifest divergence was rejected outright (2026-07-14) on layering grounds: replication code stays disk-agnostic, and CA adds no field to the Keeper part header, because a CA-specific field in ReplicatedMergeTreePartHeader would couple ReplicatedMergeTree to one disk implementation, grow the fork's upstream-contact surface, and add states to already-complex replication. Fetch-by-relink needs no Keeper field either since the manifest id travels in-band over the interserver handshake.
`ReplicatedMergeTree` is allowed on `ContentAddressed` storage; the B33-lift comment documents why the previous rejection was removed.

In the same reproduction, plain INSERT failed with the byte-identical `Code 236 ABORTED` as MERGE; the observed difference was that MERGE was re-queued by replication and recomputed about every two seconds while INSERT surfaced the error to the client.
The generic `DownloadPart` path measured approximately 15 `HEAD`s and 15 `GET`s per replicated part.

Before the queue, soak workloads reached 156 concurrent shard-mutating threads within one second, producing 637k `casPut` attempts for 380k landed mutations, a 40% average conflict rate and 92% conflict rate during storms.

The flat-combining shard queue reduced S08 contention to 8 conflicts across 702,172 mutations, while 100,000 parts were created successfully and root-shard objects stayed bounded at at most 8 per namespace.
Relink fetches consumed about 1,021,705 GETs and 1,957,163 HEADs, with zero blob-body uploads.

The relink refusal path was fail-closed and both replicas converged to identical `count`, `sum_fp`, and `sum_version`; its measured cost was CPU, log volume, and lost dedup rather than correctness loss.
`CaRelinkConfirmCore_empty_receivers.cfg` passed as green when `Receivers = {}`.

During sustained writes, `CasRefLedger::confirmExactRef` was available for approximately 17% of relink attempts, with about 92,000 refusals versus 19,531 proven confirmations in the measured sender lane.

Quorum inserts, `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA`, lost-replica recovery (`cloneReplica`), and `REPLACE_RANGE`/`DROP_RANGE` log entries all reduce to sequences of fetch (relink or byte) plus drop against a CA disk, but there is no integration test exercising them, and `cloneReplica` in particular can enqueue a large fan-out of GETs that each should relink and crosses the RPL-3/RPL-4 risk classes (RPL-5).

RPL-3 disposition (relink races GC in the shared pool): judged safe in practice because while the sender is transmitting the part and has not received an acknowledgment from the receiver, the sender cannot remove the part; the receiver gives an acknowledgment only after a successful write.
